strengths.I002-v2: Uses a new rank-1 PC1 stress prior that the absorption ratio switches on, backed by a drawdown cushion from the all-time peak and an episode-by-episode worst-case estimate (2008, 2020, 2022) with a stated 22%-in-20-days breach condition.
strengths.I003-v2: Very simple and robust: three buckets sized by inverse vol, a deadband drawdown droop, an all-time-peak backstop, and a 3.5%/day slew limit that satisfies both gates with drift margin.

verdicts.reason: I002 gives a reasoned worst-case estimate for each correlated sell-off and aims its stress prior at co-crashing assets, while I003's 20% bound rests only on the assumption that crashes unfold over 2-3 weeks.

strengths.I008-v2: Budgets risk equally across growth, duration and real classes by rule, using a crisis-day covariance, and five weekday sleeves let it trade every day with turnover headroom.
strengths.I004-v2: Has the most principled de-risking sizing: a CPPI multiplier set by a stress-floored N-1 cluster loss and a historical-simulation reserve, with asymmetric cut and restore ramps.

verdicts.reason: I004 runs at exactly 5*4% = 20% weekly turnover with no margin for drift, and at lambda=0 it can move fully to cash where its minimum-trade swap has nothing to sell, while I008's sleeves and 19.5% stop hold both gates with headroom.

strengths.I008-v2: Equalises risk contribution across the three classes using a covariance weighted toward sell-off days, and layers a trend gate, a vol target and a drawdown brake aimed at correlated stress such as 2022.
strengths.I003-v2: Few parameters and a transparent droop law with an all-time-peak backstop; it is cheap to test and plainly satisfies the gates.

verdicts.reason: I008 equalises each class's risk contribution under crisis correlations, whereas I003 equalises only standalone bucket vol, which ignores the stock-bond correlation flip that concentrates risk in 2022.

strengths.I002-v2: A cushion measured from the all-time NAV peak, with a 0.25 exposure floor and a 2% drift margin, plus explicit per-episode loss estimates and a novel PC1 stress prior.
strengths.I004-v2: A stressed-loss reserve (largest cluster plus joint historical simulation) directly sizes the CPPI multiplier, the most explicit mechanism linking exposure to a survivable 20-day loss.

verdicts.reason: I004 concedes that its rolling 504-day peak lets all-time drawdown staircase past the bound, while I002's cushion is measured from the all-time NAV peak and comes with a stated breach condition.

strengths.I003-v2: Always keeps at least 10% invested, trades daily under a 3.5% slew with drift margin, and caps staircase losses with an all-time-peak backstop, all in about 100 lines.
strengths.I004-v2: Sizes exposure by a measured, stress-floored reserve against the largest cluster loss, and adds a 200-day trend filter to cash.

verdicts.reason: I003's slew limit leaves drift headroom under 20% and never empties the book, while I004 sits exactly at the 20% cap and can go all-cash, where its daily-trade rule has nothing to trade.

strengths.I002-v2: Uses a novel absorption-ratio-scaled PC1 stress prior inside ERC, with an all-time-peak cushion and reasoned per-episode drawdown estimates.
strengths.I008-v2: Fixes risk budgets of one third per asset class by rule, computed on a crisis-day covariance, so no class dominates risk at any date.

verdicts.reason: I008 enforces equal class-level risk contributions by rule, while I002's per-asset ERC over 10 ETFs, five of them equity-like, leaves class risk share uncontrolled, and I002 even lists max class share as a test output rather than a constraint.
